name: open_high_low_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, a 5-second bar where open equals low (every tick at or above open) reveals aggressive institutional buying that absorbed all resting sell orders at that price level — the index found no sellers willing to offer below the opening price of that 5-second window. When accompanied by elevated relative volume (>1.5× the 5-minute rolling mean), it confirms a genuine demand imbalance rather than thin-market drift. Institutional TWAP algorithms executing buy orders in NIFTY futures create these patterns as they systematically lift offers, and the order typically spans multiple 5-second windows, driving the index 8-15 spot points higher over the next 30-90 seconds. The complementary open=high bar identifies the equivalent sell-side imbalance where the index found no buyers above open, signaling distribution.

indicators.name: open_eq_low_flag
indicators.purpose: Identifies 5-second bars where NIFTY never traded below its open — a direct signal of aggressive buy-side demand exhausting sell orders. Lookback is 1 (current bar only) because this is a per-bar structural property, not a rolling calculation. No scaling from the original is needed: the pattern is the same at any timeframe and we are applying it to every 5s bar intraday rather than only the first daily bar.

indicators.name: open_eq_high_flag
indicators.purpose: Identifies 5-second bars where NIFTY never traded above its open — a signal of aggressive sell-side pressure consuming all buy orders. Symmetric counterpart to open_eq_low_flag.

indicators.name: rel_volume
indicators.purpose: Volume relative to the 60-bar (5-minute) rolling mean. Original used 20 one-minute bars (20-minute window). At 5s resolution, 60 bars = 5 minutes, which is the right window to capture the current session's volume rhythm without being too slow (20+ min) or too fast (1 min). A 5-minute window tracks intraday volume cycles (opening surge, midday lull, afternoon pickup) and correctly identifies when the current 5s bar is abnormally active. We do NOT scale 12x from 20 (which would give 240 bars = 20 min) because the original's 20-min window was designed to span several trading cycles on a 1-min chart; at 5s we want the same ~5-minute cycle context.

conditions: abs(open - low) < 0.1 (open=low flag: every tick at or above open in the 5s window)
rel_volume > rel_volume_threshold (elevated demand confirms genuine institutional order flow)
vix_close < vix_max (low-volatility regime: cleaner institutional order flow, fewer false spikes)
not a doji bar (open != high to exclude flat bars where both flags fire)
buy_ce.confirmation: none — one-sided bar is a real-time microstructure signal, no lagged confirmation

conditions: abs(open - high) < 0.1 (open=high flag: every tick at or below open in the 5s window)
rel_volume > rel_volume_threshold (elevated supply confirms genuine institutional selling)
not a doji bar (open != low to exclude flat bars)

exit.stop_rationale: 3 option points (~6 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5) — if a genuine one-sided demand bar's momentum fails to continue, NIFTY should not retrace 6 spot points within 30 seconds; a deeper retrace invalidates the institutional order flow thesis and suggests the bar was a thin-market artefact rather than real demand.
exit.target_rationale: 5 option points (~10 NIFTY spot points) — institutional TWAP orders generating one-sided NIFTY bars typically drive 8-15 spot point moves over 30-90 seconds; 5 option pts captures the conservative lower end of this range, yielding 1:1.67 risk-reward vs the 3-point stop.

filters.vix_filter: vix < 21 — elevated VIX creates choppy two-sided order flow where one-sided bars are often false breakouts from retail panic rather than institutional demand
filters.volume_filter: rel_volume > 1.5 to confirm genuine order flow imbalance vs low-liquidity drift

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — one-sided bars on NIFTY 5s data are visible to all algorithmic participants; crowding risk increases as more strategies target the same microstructure events

adaptation_notes: Original applied open=high/low only to the FIRST bar of the session (09:20 first 1-minute bar) on individual FnO stocks, exploiting opening auction imbalances. On NIFTY at 5-second resolution, we generalize the pattern to all intraday bars because institutional TWAP/VWAP algorithms create one-sided bars throughout the session, not just at open. Volume baseline changed from 20-bar SMA (20-min on 1-min bars) to 60-bar rolling mean (5-min on 5s bars) to capture the current session's volume rhythm at an appropriate timescale — not 12x scaled (which would give 240 bars/20 min) but chosen to match the NIFTY intraday volume cycle. Stop/target replaced ATR-based equity exit with fixed option point stops (3/5 pts) calibrated to 30-90 second hold times. VIX filter retained at <21.
weaknesses: Open=low/high conditions are frequent on NIFTY 5s bars during thin moments — elevated volume filter is critical; without it, signal count would be extremely high and win rate would collapse
Flat doji bars (open=high=low) fire both flags simultaneously and must be excluded explicitly
In strongly trending markets, multiple consecutive one-sided bars signal continuation but strategy exits at the first target, capping trend-following upside
NIFTY volume in the 5s data can be noisy or zero during pre-open/post-close periods; session filter essential
